chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Working at Cafe Society with Tatum; Barney Josephson
summary: Stewart worked there twice with Tatum without feeling bothered, remembers Josephson as a nice person, and Crouch says its success opened 52nd Street clubs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And so he said that was when he started the club. But you later worked there?
I later worked there with Art Tatum, yes.
Did you work there often?
Oh, I think I worked there twice.
How did you feel working in that kind of a situation?
Well, I didn't feel anything, what I mean. I just went along with the program. Of course, I was so wrapped up in my music, you know, I just didn't -- it didn't bother me at all.
But you had noticed though as a player, now --
I had noticed, yes, oh sure, yes.
Did Tatum have anything to say about the club?
No, no. What I mean, he was -- all of us were right on the scene doing our thing.
Uh-huh. Did you -- do you remember Barney Josephson, who was the owner of the club?
Yes, I remember him, yes.
What kind of a guy was he at that time?
Quite a fellow, beautiful cat, you might say, and he treated us real nice, down-to-earth, you know. In fact, isn't he the same Barney that has --
The Cookery, yeah.
-- The Cookery? As of today, yes, right.
Yeah, the same.
I think he had another place, was involved in another place on 52nd Street. I'm not sure, but --
He may have. I know he had the Cafe Society Uptown.
Uptown, yes.
He said that that -- after the other club owners saw that you could be successful with an integrated -- or with an open policy, so to speak, as far as patrons were concerned, --
Right, right.
-- that then suddenly, clubs on 52nd Street said, 'Well, if I'm assured of getting the white dollars and I can also get the black dollars, then why not get them both?'
That's right, sure.
In fact, that's what he said, that when the Cafe Society Uptown became a success, New York -- 52nd
Street opened, was wide open then.
Right.
